title: Direct measurement of CO2 solubility and pH in NaCl hydrothermal solutions by combining in-situ potentiometry and Raman spectroscopy up to 280 C and 150 bar
authors: Laurent Truche, Elena F. Bazarkina, Gilles Berger, Marie-Camille Caumon, Gilles Bessaque, Jean Dubessy
experimental_method: 450 mL titanium hydrothermal cell with in-situ Raman spectroscopy and a Cu/Cu2O/ZrO2(Y2O3) potentiometric pH probe; dissolved inorganic carbon of sampled aliquots determined gravimetrically as BaCO3 (CO2 molality), Raman peak area ratio CO2/H2O calibrated against it.
uncertainties_stated: Temperature held within +-1 C; pH uncertainty +-0.05 (acidic) and +-0.10 (alkaline); Raman wavenumber accuracy +-0.4 cm-1; gravimetric data mostly within +-2 sigma of the Duan and Sun (2003) model; pressure uncertainty not stated.
quality_remarks: Only 12 of 21 state points have a gravimetric mCO2 (column c): 7 of 14 in pure water, 5 of 7 in 1.4 m NaCl; the others are 'nd' and the table gives only calculated molalities (Duan-Sun, Pitzer model of this paper) plus measured pH and Raman ratio. Authors say probe drift at 280 C is larger (about 0.10 pH/24 h) and the Pitzer model is confirmed at least to 250 C. 1.4 m NaCl pH fit rests on two control points.
